analysis.evidence: יֶרֶד is the subject of וַיְחִי. The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת־חֲנוֹךְ sets the starting point at the birth of Enoch, and שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה gives the eight hundred years Jared lived thereafter.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for יֶרֶד linked to the consonantal root ירד.
draft.definition: Jared is the personal name of Mahalalel’s son in Genesis 5:15.
draft.evidence: וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת יָרֶד means “he fathered Jared.” The genealogy identifies the bearer and gives no explanation of the name’s origin.

analysis.evidence: יֶרֶד is the subject of וַיְחִי, “Jared lived.” אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת חֲנוֹךְ, “after he fathered Enoch,” identifies him as Enoch’s father in the genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי introduces הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת חֲנוֹךְ, “his fathering Enoch.” Jared lived eight hundred years after that event.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת־חֲנוֹךְ means “after he fathered Enoch.” The suffix identifies Jared as the father, and אֶת marks Enoch as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular subject suffix וֹ referring to Jared.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת חֲנוֹךְ (‘after he fathered Enoch’), אֶת marks the proper name חֲנוֹךְ as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת חֲנוֹךְ, “after he fathered Enoch,” the suffix on הוֹלִידוֹ refers to Jared, and אֶת marks Enoch as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁמֹנֶה counts the hundreds (מֵאוֹת), giving the eight hundred years Jared lived after fathering Enoch.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: eight as the multiplier of hundreds

analysis.evidence: שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה means “eight hundred years.” שְׁמֹנֶה counts the hundreds in the span Jared lived after fathering Enoch.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה counts the eight hundred years Jared lived after he fathered Enoch. The singular noun supplies the unit for this span of his life.
Jared (יֶרֶד) is the subject. The direct objects בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת, “sons and daughters,” identify the children he fathered.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix
